newsitem.title: USA: HFS, CUC in definitive merger pact. [CORRECTED 23:22 GMT]
newsitem.headline: HFS, CUC in definitive merger pact. [CORRECTED 23:22 GMT]

text.p: CUC International Inc and HFS Inc said Tuesday they reached a definitive agreement to merge in a deal that would create a consumer and business services company with a market capitalization of $22 billion.

The companies, in a joint statement, said CUC would issue about 434 million shares, valued at about $11 billion, in exchange for all HFS Inc's shares outstanding in a ratio of 2.4031 CUC shares for each HFS share.

The merger, which will be accounted for as a pooling of interests, links CUC's membership-based direct marketing business with HFS's brand-name operations that include auto rental company Avis, the Days Inn and Ramada hotel chains and the Coldwell Banker and Century 21 real estate businesses.
The combined company will have revenues of about $4.3 billion, net income of nearly $600 million and free cash flow of about $700 million based on pro forma performance in calendar 1996, they said.
Calling the deal a merger of equals, the companies said their top executives would share leadership of the combined company, which has yet to be named.

At first, HFS chairman and chief executive Henry Silverman will serve as president and chief executive of the new company and CUC chairman and chief executive Walter Forbes will be chairman. The two will switch titles on January 1, 2001.
HFS and CUC will share equal representation on the new board.
Both companies will maintain their respective operations and said they expect no job cuts as a result of the deal.
The deal follows by less than a month HFS's stock swap merger with PHH Corp. HFS is also involved tangentially in Hilton Hotels Corp's ongoing battle for control of ITT Corp.
HFS made no reference to the Hilton-ITT matter, but Hilton said today's deal "did not appear" to alter HFS's role in the ITT bid.
Under terms of their agreement -- assuming Hilton's hostile bid for ITT succeeds -- Hilton would license the Sheraton name to HFS.
(Corrects to indicate that HFS would license the Sheraton name but would not operate ITT's hotels).
